mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in residential investment (RSAFS) signals strong household spending and confidence, which translates into higher corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring any threshold condition.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 3.0% and remains above this level for two consecutive months, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 3.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days only when both conditions are met.
failure_condition: The joint movement of UNRATE declining and PAYEMS increasing fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0, which signals a manufacturing slowdown, the S&P 500 tends to underperform as corporate earnings growth weakens, but this effect is only pronounced in the early stages of a recession (as indicated by rising unemployment).
failure_condition: In early recession periods (UNRATE > 4.0% and GDPC1 growth < 0.0% in prior quarter), INDPRO < 105.0 is followed by positive 60-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A rising Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year indicates persistent inflation, which typically leads to higher interest rates and reduced equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring a specific threshold on the rate of change.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL is above 2.5% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 1,200,000 units annually, it signals strong consumer confidence and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST > 1200.0, the S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a robust labor market and manufacturing sector, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days only when both series move in the specified directions.
failure_condition: The joint movement of UNRATE declining and INDPRO increasing fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong manufacturing growth (INDPRO above 110.0), the S&P 500 tends to rise as corporate profits expand, but this effect is most pronounced in the middle of the business cycle (as indicated by stable unemployment).
failure_condition: In mid-cycle expansion (UNRATE < 4.0% and GDP growth positive), INDPRO > 110.0 is followed by negative 20-day S&P 500 returns in more than 55% of cases.
